label: Quadric Line Complex
notes: Open the chapter. The quadric line complex is a classical concrete object: the set of lines in three-dimensional projective space cut out by a single quadric on the Plucker quadric. The deck follows printed pages 733 through 804. The chapter exercises the techniques of the previous chapters on this single concrete subject.

label: Lines in P^3
notes: Set up lines in projective three-space. The Grassmannian of lines in P^3 is a four-dimensional projective variety, and the Plucker embedding realizes it as a smooth quadric in P^5. Points on this quadric are in bijection with lines in P^3, and the geometry of the quadric encodes incidence relations among the lines.

label: Plucker Embedding
notes: Walk through the Plucker embedding. Given a line spanned by two points with homogeneous coordinates, the six pairwise minors form a point in P^5. These coordinates satisfy a single quadratic Plucker relation. The image is a smooth four-dimensional quadric, the Klein quadric, and is the Grassmannian of lines.

label: Quadric Line Complex
notes: Define the quadric line complex. Intersect the Klein quadric with a second generic quadric in P^5 to obtain a smooth three-dimensional intersection. This is the quadric line complex. It parametrizes a special family of lines in P^3 and is a classical object in nineteenth-century algebraic geometry.

label: Hodge Numbers
notes: Compute Hodge numbers of the quadric line complex. By Lefschetz hyperplane theorem applied to intersections in P^5, the cohomology in low degrees matches the ambient quadric. The middle cohomology carries interesting Hodge structure; the chapter uses Picard-Lefschetz arguments to track its monodromy and identifies the Hodge diamond explicitly.

label: Applications
notes: Cover applications. The quadric line complex appears in moduli of K3 surfaces, in mirror symmetry constructions, and as a testing ground for general intersection-theoretic arguments. The chapter uses it to make concrete the abstract techniques developed in chapters 03 and 04.

label: Recap
notes: Close by recapping. The quadric line complex is a three-dimensional smooth Fano variety arising as a complete intersection in the Klein quadric. It encodes lines in P^3 subject to a quadratic condition. The chapter demonstrates how the abstract machinery of intersection theory, Hodge structures, and monodromy applies to a concrete classical example.
